# Vendored crates

The Sleigh crates this engine is built on, owned and built from this tree.
Each was copied from the commit below with only the files its own `include`
list packages; local changes are listed, and a refresh re-applies them.

| Crate | Upstream | Taken from | Local changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `libsla` 1.2.0 | github.com/mnemonikr/libsla, via the 0verflowme fork | `ebf92321` | user-operation names and the parser-cache reset (libsla#18, #19); `GhidraSleigh` reads its address spaces once, a space's name is interned, and the p-code emit reads each varnode in place and its space from that list (ROADMAP PF1; 0verflowme/libsla#1) |
| `libsla-sys` 0.1.5 | github.com/mnemonikr/libsla-sys, via the 0verflowme fork | `2ddd71ac` (Ghidra `aed1cf1c`) | the same two passthroughs (libsla-sys#8, #9); `getVarnodeSpace` and `getVarnodeOffset`, which read a varnode where `getAddress` allocated an `Address` (0verflowme/libsla-sys#1); Ghidra's include directory stated as `DEP_SLA_INCLUDE` (#2); Ghidra's decompiler C++ only; Ghidra: `SleighBase` keeps the context fields `buildXrefs` found, so `reregisterContext` walks no symbol table, `Sleigh` records whether a decode committed context and can mark its cached parses stale, and the bridge's `clearCache` rebuilds the context only after a commit (ROADMAP PF0; 0verflowme/libsla-sys#3 over 0verflowme/ghidra `r2sleigh-sleigh-context`); `cc`'s `parallel` feature, so the C++ sources compile concurrently (audit B1; 0verflowme/libsla-sys#4); built at `opt-level = 3` in dev and release by the root `Cargo.toml`, including as the spec compiler's build dependency (audit B2) |
| `sleigh-compiler` 2.0.2 | github.com/mnemonikr/sleigh-compiler | crates.io 2.0.2 | builds against `libsla-sys`'s Ghidra sources (`DEP_SLA_INCLUDE`, which `libsla-sys` states) instead of its own copy, since it links that `libsla` and must see the same class layouts (0verflowme/sleigh-compiler#1, 0verflowme/libsla-sys#2); built at `opt-level = 3` as a build dependency by the root `Cargo.toml`, which cuts the SLA compile from about 29 s to 11–14 s (audit B2) |
| `sleigh-config` 1.0.1 | github.com/mnemonikr/sleigh-config, via the 0verflowme fork | `71551911` | only the processors the workspace enables (x86, ARM, AARCH64, MIPS, RISCV) and their features; each processor's files by name with its `.ldefs` and `.dwarf` (0verflowme/sleigh-config#1); Ghidra's Go compiler specifications corrected to Go's `abi-internal.md`: on x86-64, RDX (the closure context, scratch at return) is no longer unaffected and X8 to X14 carry float arguments; on AArch64, the return address is x30, a call shifts the stack by nothing, x16 and x17 (scratch, used by linker trampolines) are no longer unaffected, and x18 (reserved), x28 (the goroutine) and x29 (the frame pointer) are (ROADMAP LP1; 0verflowme/sleigh-config#2); AArch64 `addv` to a B register zeroes the 31 bytes above it (`zext_zb`), where Ghidra 11.4 zeroed only those above the Q register and left the source lanes in bytes 1 to 15 (0verflowme/sleigh-config#3); resynced from Ghidra master (918acd744d), hunk by hunk: `ldpsw`'s second word at +4 (bbe8d7ca93), `ldapr Xt` loads (b5fb4d36ed), `ldar Wt` loads 4 bytes (3fbe33860b), `stlrb`/`stlrh` store 1 and 2 (d0650fa0ef), scalar `fmadd`/`fmsub` and the byte reductions zero the vector above their result (59c854e0e9, b4c3c95490), `eor3`, `bcax`, `rax1` and `xar` (51bd4207a0, GP-7313); a W-form sign-extending load (`ldrsb`, `ldrsh`, `ldursb`, `ldursh`, `ldtrsb`) sign-extends to 32 bits and zeroes the upper 32, the shape of Ghidra PRs #6471 and #6447; a W-, H- or B-destination LSE atomic, `cas`, `casp`, `ldapr`, `ldlar` or `swp` writes the whole X register zero-extended, and `ldsmin`/`ldsmax`/`ldumin`/`ldumax` B and H compare at the access size; `mrs`/`msr nzcv` read and write the four flags, and `crc32*` passes its polynomial as a constant, not a load from the constant space; `stlxp` stores its second register at +8; scalar FP rounding rounds as each instruction states (`frintm`/`frintp`/`frintz` and `fcvtms`/`fcvtps` exactly, `frinta`/`frintn`/`fcvtas`/`fcvtns` by a floor-and-compare sequence, `frinti`/`frintx` as named operations, unsigned `fcvt` split at 2^63) and scalar `fmax`/`fmin`/`fmaxnm` call the operations the vector forms do; the specifications and the tables that list them are `static`, so a non-LTO build embeds each once (audit B3; 0verflowme/sleigh-config#11); one `sla-<stem>` feature per `.slaspec` in place of the processor features, and only the selected specifications are compiled and embedded, the languages r2sleigh-lift's features read (audit B4; 0verflowme/sleigh-config#12, where the processor features are kept beside them) |
